description: Condition-matched enrollment ablation: simulated vs genuine narrowband
key_finding: Genuine phone-degraded audio with condition matching achieves 14.6% BETTER SEPARATION (0.5268 vs 0.4596) than ffmpeg-simulated degradation. However, BOTH lose separation vs not doing condition matching (0.6367 baseline). Genuine phone narrowband is more distinctive than simulated, but a single wideband centroid may be more robust than condition-matched approaches.

wideband_baseline.description: Baseline: genuine narrowband probe vs enrolled wideband centroid (mismatch, no condition awareness)
wideband_baseline.genuine_description: phone-degraded audio scored against wideband centroid

simulated_matched.description: Condition-matched with simulated degradation: genuine narrowband probe vs ffmpeg-degraded centroid
simulated_matched.genuine_description: phone-degraded probe scored against centroid from ffmpeg-degraded wideband
simulated_matched.note: Centroid created by degrading wideband enrollment with ffmpeg

genuine_matched.description: Condition-matched with genuine audio: genuine narrowband probe vs genuine narrowband centroid
genuine_matched.genuine_description: phone-degraded probe scored against centroid from genuine phone-degraded audio
genuine_matched.note: Centroid created from friend_test_nb8k_enroll.wav (genuine phone audio)

interpretation.genuine_vs_simulated: Genuine phone-degraded audio is 14.6% MORE DISTINCTIVE when matched against a centroid created from similar phone audio than when compared against a centroid from computationally-simulated degradation.
interpretation.condition_matching_trade: Condition-matched enrollment trades absolute separation for acoustic-condition specificity. A narrowband probe loses 17-28% separation when compared against condition-matched centroids vs a generic wideband centroid.
interpretation.robustness_vs_specificity: Single wideband centroid achieves best separation but ignores probe condition. Condition-matched enrollment with genuine audio achieves better separation than simulated, but at cost of lower absolute separation.
interpretation.recommendation: For this speaker and test set, a single wideband centroid is most robust. Condition-matching adds value only when degradation characteristics matter more than raw separation (e.g., applications where phone calls are common and reproducibility matters).
